Kuils River Pollution.

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The impact of the pollution and the experiences of people living alongside Cape Town's Kuils River is described as "Apocalyptic" by experts.

Unique Selling Point:
For years, scientists and the communities living next to the Kuils River near Macassar CT, have expressed concern that the sewage flowing into the river from a nearby waste water treatment plant is both an environmental and a health hazard. The people of Sandvlei below the discharge point from the Zandvliet facility, are suffering from numerous medical complaints so severe that they have even resulted in surgical intervention due to E.coli poisoning. The City of Cape Town claimed for many years that the facility only discharges treated effluent. However recently the council conceded that "sub-standard" treated effluent is leaving the plant. Nothing has been done about it. Chemicals and the effluent have also had a detrimental effect of marine life in False Bay.

Summary:
The City of Cape Town is undertaking a health survey to investigate the concerns of the community. A step long overdue. How long it will take the council to act is not known. The City denies that its handling of sewage is negligent.
The pollution has impacted on marine life in False Bay. Ibuprofen has been found in huge levels in snoek. Pharmaceutical products aren't the only substances which can't be adequately processed by plants such as Zandvliet. There are findings of traces of caffeine in sea urchins.
The City of Cape Town claims the problem is caused by informal settlements and unplanned development by residents of the catchment area which extends northwards from Khayelitsha towards Kuils River. The human waste from these "illegal settlements" and Cape Town's rapid population growth is also contributing to the contamination of the river.

Further information:
The Zandvliet Plant was designed with technology that was available 20.30 years ago. the Zandvliet plant was built before many of the new chemicals which currently flood sewage systems were introduced. It is incapable of adequately breaking them down. These chemicals are then washed out into the ocean and contaminate marine Life.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel to CP - Producer and Presenter.
Car hire.
Accommodation for 1 night.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The impact of the pollution and the experiences of people living alongside Cape Town's Kuils River is described as "Apocalyptic" by experts.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: For years, scientists and the communities living next to the Kuils River near Macassar CT, have expressed concern that the sewage flowing into the river from a nearby waste water treatment plant is both an environmental and a health hazard. The people of Sandvlei below the discharge point from the Zandvliet facility, are suffering from numerous medical complaints so severe that they have even resulted in surgical intervention due to E.coli poisoning. The City of Cape Town claimed for many years that the facility only discharges treated effluent. However recently the council conceded that "sub-standard" treated effluent is leaving the plant. Nothing has been done about it. Chemicals and the effluent have also had a detrimental effect of marine life in False Bay.
metadata.Summary: The City of Cape Town is undertaking a health survey to investigate the concerns of the community. A step long overdue. How long it will take the council to act is not known. The City denies that its handling of sewage is negligent. The pollution has impacted on marine life in False Bay. Ibuprofen has been found in huge levels in snoek. Pharmaceutical products aren't the only substances which can't be adequately processed by plants such as Zandvliet. There are findings of traces of caffeine in sea urchins. The City of Cape Town claims the problem is caused by informal settlements and unplanned development by residents of the catchment area which extends northwards from Khayelitsha towards Kuils River. The human waste from these "illegal settlements" and Cape Town's rapid population growth is also contributing to the contamination of the river.
metadata.Further information: The Zandvliet Plant was designed with technology that was available 20.30 years ago. the Zandvliet plant was built before many of the new chemicals which currently flood sewage systems were introduced. It is incapable of adequately breaking them down. These chemicals are then washed out into the ocean and contaminate marine Life.
